current.text: He has a hamstring injury. He missed the preseason and will be re-evaluated in week one. One note says he might miss one or two games, or none. Yahoo lists him as questionable.
Grayson Allen starts in his place while he is out.
current.until: Knueppel returns from the hamstring injury

current.text: LaMelo Ball and Miles Bridges are gone from Charlotte. Knueppel is a projected starter with Coby White, Brandon Miller, Naz Reid and Moussa Diabate.
His usage should rise from 22% to about 24 or 25%, in about 32 minutes. Experts expect more shots, more threes, more assists and more turnovers.

He is one of the candidates to take on creation duties. One preview expects him to carry more of the creation load than Brandon Miller. Playmaking should be spread across White, Knueppel and Miller, and how they split it is the big question for their efficiency.
Experts expect his shooting efficiency to drop without LaMelo Ball setting him up. One thinks people overrate how much Ball's exit helps him.

Experts agree he is overvalued at an ADP in the 30s and 40s. They value him in the 60s to 70s and say not to take him in rounds 3 or 4 or in the top 50. One would take him at an ESPN rank near 91. One doubts he will beat last season's category rank.
In an auction mock draft, Josh would not pay more than 8 USD for him. He went for 13 USD.
Charlotte plays 4-3-4 games in our playoff weeks (March 28 end) and has only 13 back-to-backs, the league minimum.
Charlotte plans to space the floor and take a lot of threes.

durable.text: His threes made are a league outlier. He made 3.4 threes a game on 42% as a rookie. FT% is also a clear strength.
He does little beyond points and threes. He gets almost no steals or blocks and is not a big rebounder.
His shooting was great overall as a rookie (48% FG, 42% from three), but not in the games he played without LaMelo Ball.
As a rookie he had an ADP of 111 and finished 66th in category leagues. He faded over the final two months (91st), a partial rookie wall.
His game is worth more in category leagues than in points leagues. He was 66th in 9-cat and 89th in points last season.

note: Experts agree he is overpriced at an ADP in the 30s and 40s and value him in the 60s. Yahoo's 9.5 USD average cost fits that better than ESPN's 14.9 USD (Yahoo values him at 16 USD), and one expert's mock ceiling was 8 USD. He is a clear 3PM and FT% asset for builds that chase threes, but he brings almost no steals or blocks. Early on, check how his hamstring recovers, how his usage grows and whether his 47% FG holds up without LaMelo Ball.
